issues.description: validate_conda substring match on --version output mis-identifies impostors.
issues.detail: The validator returns True if 'conda', 'mamba', or 'micromamba' appears anywhere in lowercased --version output. Any binary printing those substrings (anaconda-build, paths like /opt/anaconda/bin/foo) passes. Match on the leading token of the version string or check the basename.

issues.description: validate_conda returns True for the empty string, conflating unset with valid.
issues.detail: Returning True for '' so the preferences field does not flag empty input violates the advertised postcondition ('points to a working conda executable'). Callers cannot trust the function name. Split the contract (is_empty vs is_valid) or have the UI layer decide that empty means unset.

issues.description: File browser filter '*.exe' is unconditional and breaks Linux/macOS.
issues.detail: On Linux and macOS, conda/mamba/micromamba executables have no extension. Hardcoding '*.exe' as the file dialog filter gives non-Windows users an empty picker by default. Platform-gate the filter on sys.platform or drop it.

issues.description: kernelspec argv() uses the custom conda_path without re-validating at use time.
issues.detail: When custom_conda is True, conda_path is consumed directly; only a falsy value triggers the error path. A path that was valid at config time may be stale, missing, or no longer executable. Re-check on use and surface a precise error pointing at the preference.

issues.description: run_program subprocess in validate_conda has no timeout and leaks the process handle.
issues.detail: run_program(...).communicate() captures stdout but the Popen is discarded without timeout, returncode check, or explicit pipe close. A hung or misidentified binary blocks the preferences UI thread, and live validation per keystroke leaks descriptors. Bind the process, add a timeout, and close cleanly.

issues.description: setFocus() added to shared create_browsefile helper changes behavior for every caller.
issues.detail: create_browsefile is shared infrastructure used by many preference pages. Adding edit.setFocus() after select_file alters focus behavior site-wide, not just for the conda case. Move the focus call to the conda-specific caller instead of the shared widget.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this PR adds a useful user-configurable conda executable but ships with a sloppy validator and a Windows-only file filter. validate_conda's contract is broken in two ways: substring matching on --version admits impostors, and the empty string is reported as valid. The kernelspec consumer trusts the persisted path without re-validating at use time, and the file dialog filter '*.exe' breaks Linux/macOS users. Secondary cleanups: subprocess needs a timeout and proper cleanup, and the shared browsefile helper should not gain a setFocus side effect. Verdict: needs-work but fixable; tighten the validator, gate the filter, and re-check at use time.
